coverage.claim: Nonvanishing of finite products needed to define omitted-node barycentric weights and the node polynomial off the nodes
Finite products of quotients are quotients of the corresponding products, including the empty list; this justifies the scalar-times-monic-polynomial form of each cardinal function
Finite double-sum interchange used to construct the coefficient vector of the cardinal interpolant
Cardinal functions, their coefficient-list degree and node-value properties, and the unique degree-at-most-n interpolant
Highest derivative of a polynomial and the pointwise Lagrange remainder with a fully checked higher-Rolle application
Exact barycentric denominator/numerator identities and separate evaluation at a node
Equispaced cardinal basis lower bound proportional to the degree for data varying with degree
Finite checked-arithmetic control flow and termination with explicit status
Forward-error, conditioning, or accuracy certification for the rounded evaluator
coverage.reason: The algorithm states no such guarantee; the cited floating-point article warns that the arithmetic behavior depends on node distribution, and the numerical claim requires a separate analysis.

coverage.claim: Exact quadratic interpolation at the nodes -1, 0, and 1
Equality in the pointwise remainder formula for a cubic and three nodes
Linear cardinal-basis amplification for unit-bounded nodal data, stated separately from fixed-function divergence
Spline interpolation, fixed-function convergence, and rounded-evaluation error bounds
coverage.reason: These belong to distinct spline, approximation, or finite-precision claims and are not asserted by this examples page.

resolution_note: The stale design bibliography also named Trefethen's ATAP first6.pdf and a Duke interpolation handout; the recorded initial shell fetches returned HTTP 404.
